chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Sa'd Bayya' al-Sabiri, who said:
I said to Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: “Should a man force himself to weep in salat (prayer)?” He said: “Excellent, excellent, even if it be like the head of a fly.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as meaning that he intended when one weeps out of خشية of Allah, not that he should weep for something from the afflictions of the world; that is indicated by what supports this.

key_terms.أَيَتَبَاكَى: to make oneself weep or induce crying
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer in which this ruling is discussed
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ مَحْمُولٌ عَلَى: the report is interpreted and applied in a specific qualified sense
key_terms.بَخٍّ بَخٍّ: an expression of praise and approval
key_terms.خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ: reverent fear and awe of Allah that motivates valid weeping
key_terms.رَأْسِ الذُّبَابِ: a metaphor for an extremely small amount
key_terms.مَصَائِبِ الدُّنْيَا: worldly afflictions, excluded here as the cause of weeping in prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to make oneself cry during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the permissibility and merit of inducing tears in salat (prayer), even if only to a very slight degree. The compiler clarifies that this applies to weeping arising from خشية of Allah, not weeping over worldly misfortunes during the prayer.
